title: dynamic-egress-multipath-module-with-az-aware-route-lifecycle
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a new Terraform module that provides AZ-aware, multipath egress for private deployments. The module should support configurable egress strategies (single NAT, HA NAT, Internet Gateway with route priority, multipath egress using regional endpoints), automated health-driven route reconciliation, and lifecycle hooks to enable safe upgrades with minimal traffic disruption.
proposed_solution: Develop a reusable module (redwood_vpc_egress) exposing inputs for subnet groups, az_preferences, nat_strategy, endpoint_definitions, and upgrade_policy. The module will manage: (1) deterministic route tables per AZ with route weights, (2) optional HA NAT Gateway sets with automatic blackhole detection and promotion, (3) regional VPC endpoints (S3/DynamoDB/STS) attached to private route tables, (4) a lightweight Lambda health probe that updates a Route State resource via Terraform provider or SSM param for reconciliation. Add a toggle for blue/green NAT replacements: create secondary NAT set, warm it, switch routes atomically, then destroy old NATs. Provide outputs for egress_ips, route_table_ids, and a generated migration plan file stored in S3 for audit.
acceptance_criteria: Module published to internal registry with semantic versioning and changelog
Supports inputs: public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_map, az_ordering, nat_strategy, endpoint_list, enable_flow_logs
Smoke tests validate outbound connectivity to S3 and external internet from each AZ after deployment
Health probe detects and fails over a blackholed NAT gateway within configured probe_interval
Upgrade path tested: blue/green NAT replacement completes with zero dropped requests for 99% of connections during warmup window
Route reconciliation job runs and corrects stale/blackholed routes within SLA (configurable)
notes: Trade-offs considered: maintaining full HA NAT per AZ increases cost but reduces cross-AZ egress latency and avoids asymmetric paths for TCP-heavy workloads.
We prefer deterministic per-AZ routing over cross-AZ shared NAT to avoid bursty inter-AZ data transfer and preserve SLOs for latency-sensitive inference traffic.
Potential future extension: integrate with Dedicated capacity placement so model-serving subnets can be pinned to specific egress profiles.
implementation_steps: Design module interface and variable schema; publish RFC doc to Confluence: /confluence/redwood/vpc-egress-multipath
Create Terraform module scaffold with examples for single-az, multi-az-ha, and multipath configurations
Implement route table generation per AZ and route weighting via AWS route priority + blackhole detection tags
Add Lambda health probe (Go) and IAM role; probe reports to SSM parameter and optional SNS for alerts
Implement blue/green NAT workflow using lifecycle hooks and plan artifact stored in S3
Write acceptance/integration tests: terratest + end-to-end connectivity checks; include chaos test to simulate NAT failure
Create GitHub PR with CHANGELOG and update internal registry; run rollout in staging then 1 production region as canary
Document upgrade runbook and rollback steps in repo README and runbook playbook
testing_and_validation: Terratest suite: create temporary VPC -> deploy module -> run connectivity tests to S3 and internet
Chaos scenario: kill NAT ENI/attach fake route blackhole and assert route reconciliation fixes within probe_interval
Canary rollout in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with traffic shaping to measure latency/regression
Cost estimate report per config (single NAT vs per-AZ HA vs multipath) generated by terraform-cost-estimator
